slides.title: Galaxy General Unveils Self-Learning Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The introduction of a self-learning humanoid robot demonstrates an inflection point in embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Towards Actionable Surgical Team Dynamics: from Teamwork to Counterfactual Annotations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal dataset featuring speaker diarization and annotations of group dynamics and interaction processes, supporting HyECHO's focus on social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Introduces an extended multimodal surgical dataset with multi-level teamwork and counterfactual annotations to analyze team dynamics.
card.key_idea: Enriches the MM-OR dataset with speaker diarization, bilingual transcripts, and a hierarchical annotation framework (team, interaction, individual levels) plus counterfactual breakdown triggers.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via expert human annotations across 169 samples using standardized protocols (OTAS, HMT, NOTSS, BFTQ, SYMLOG, GLIS) with inter-rater analysis.
card.limitation: Moderate class imbalance in ratings, as recorded surgical teams generally demonstrated acceptable performance, making extreme ratings rare.

slides.authors: Vincenzo Marco De Luca et al.

slides.title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZATION IN EMG-IMU ACTIVITY RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research introduces the MAGIC-HRI dataset for recognizing human activities and gestures to support object-handover and assembly scenarios. It demonstrates that personalization is likely required for robust deployment in HRI due to significant subject dependence in EMG and IMU signals, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Personalization is essential for robust EMG-IMU activity recognition in HRI due to high inter-subject variability.
card.key_idea: Introduces MAGIC-HRI dataset (53 classes) using Random Forest on time/frequency features, demonstrating that injecting a few subject-specific samples significantly improves Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) performance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 11 subjects using LOSO and 75/25 splits. Random Forest performed best; personalization increased F1-score to >65% with 7 samples.
card.limitation: Lacks online robot-in-the-loop evaluation and shows a large generalization gap without subject-specific calibration.

slides.authors: Ruan Rithelle Chagas de Faria Carminati et al.

slides.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal Turkish corpus with synchronized video and audio to predict turn-taking dynamics, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Introduces Real-TurnTurk, a multimodal Turkish corpus for predicting turn-taking transitions in natural conversations.
card.key_idea: A Genetic Algorithm optimizes interpretable AND-OR decision rules using 28 visual, acoustic, and linguistic features to classify turn-change points.
card.evaluation: 5-fold cross-validation on 11 dyadic interactions. The GA rule achieved F1=57.0%, modestly outperforming silence thresholds and an always-positive baseline.
card.limitation: Small dataset size (11 conversations) and speaker-level imbalance prevent fully speaker-disjoint evaluation and claims of statistical significance.

slides.title: LLM-Based Selection of Incongruent Verbal and Nonverbal Behavior for Virtual Humans
slides.highlight: This work explores how LLMs can select mismatched verbal and nonverbal behaviors based on social context, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: LLMs can generate realistic, incongruent verbal and nonverbal behaviors for virtual humans using context-rich prompting.
card.key_idea: A taxonomy of verbal-nonverbal mismatches (e.g., irony, deception) was used to test three prompting levels: utterance only, dialogue history, and dialogue plus situational context.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Claude-3.5-Sonnet output analysis and two human-subject studies (N=49 and N=39) using virtual human videos and Likert scales.
card.limitation: The system lacks gestures, postural shifts, and voice prosody, and requires manual mapping of LLM descriptions to animation parameters.

slides.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME ONLINE MOTOR LEARNING VIA FREE-ENERGY-GATED PLASTICITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) to enable robots to acquire and retain motor patterns during real-time physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A gated plasticity mechanism enables robots to learn multiple motor patterns online without catastrophic forgetting.
card.key_idea: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) scales synaptic updates using a sigmoidal function of variational free energy, increasing plasticity during model-environment mismatch and suppressing it during stability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via prerecorded streams and real-time pHRI using a dual-arm robot; metrics included repertoire coverage and retention across 50 sessions per condition.

slides.title: Minimal Local Simulation Foundations for LLM- and VLM-Driven Agents in 2D and 3D Environments
slides.tldr: MINIMAL SIMULATION FOUNDATIONS FOR LLM/VLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces SD-AgentFoundry-2D and SD-AgentFoundry-3D, providing accessible foundations for generative social simulation and agent-based behaviors, which aligns with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: Two minimal, locally-hosted simulation foundations for prototyping LLM-driven 2D social and VLM-driven 3D embodied agents.
card.key_idea: SD-AgentFoundry-2D uses LLMs for grid-based communication and movement; SD-AgentFoundry-3D uses VLMs with USD assets for first-person visual grounding and natural-language action interpretation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via qualitative representative runs (2D fire scenario, 3D logo search). Not a controlled benchmark or predictive validity study.
card.limitation: Not a trained VLA policy; cannot learn motor skills, handle contact-rich manipulation, or close high-frequency sensorimotor loops.

slides.title: Dual-Scale State-Space Modeling with Speaker-Wise Dynamic CRF for Speech Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work proposes DSSM-CRF to model cross-speaker influence and within-speaker emotion evolution, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: DSSM-CRF improves conversational speech emotion recognition using dual-scale state-space modeling and speaker-specific dynamic CRF decoding.
card.key_idea: Bidirectional state-space models encode frame and dialogue scales, while a speaker-wise dynamic CRF separates individual emotion trajectories from cross-speaker contextual influences using pair-conditioned transition residuals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP (75.81% UA) and MELD (54.72% WA) against various baselines; results are supported by component ablations and backbone comparisons.
card.limitation: Abrupt within-speaker emotion changes (shifts) remain significantly harder to predict than emotion persistence (inertia).

slides.title: Georgia Southern University Unveils State-of-the-Art Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The introduction of a state-of-the-art humanoid robot at Georgia Southern University is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.
